> This notebook brings all upstream optimization work together to identify the
> best overall layout to use for this edition. Result is saved as a package
> dataset, see `help(best_layout)`.



# Summary of upstream work

In `vignette("layout_candidates")`, we identified 7
layouts candidates with:

- whole-pica text widths that yield 44--66 characters per line
- whole-line text heights that produce a harmoniously proportioned text block
- page dimensions and margins that produce harmonious proportions for all
  rectangles of positive & negative space on the two-page spread

In `vignette("hj_optimization")`, we performed a grid search of typesetting
parameters that control hyphenation and justification. For each candidate text
width, we identified the set of typesetting parameters that produces justified
text with the least distorted word space. No solutions were found for a
15-pica
text width, leaving us with 6 layout candidates moving
forward.

In `vignette("page_break_optimization")`, we performed a chapter-by-chapter grid
search of typesetting parameters that control page breaks and vertical space.
There were 53 solutions that can be set with available
metal type and have zero underfull lines, overfull lines, widows, orphans,
hyphenated page breaks, broken quotations, or broken chapter transitions. Only
4 layout candidates remain.



# Selecting the best layout

Let's begin by picking a single best option for each layout candidate. We get
slightly different sets depending on whether we favor consistent word space or
consistent vertical space around chapter transitions. For thoroughness, let's
consider both.


``` r
best_pagination_proofs <- bind_rows(
  pagination_proofs |>
    slice_min(by = "layout_id", word_space_rmse) |>
    slice_min(by = "layout_id", ch_vspace_sd),
  pagination_proofs |>
    slice_min(by = "layout_id", ch_vspace_sd) |>
    slice_min(by = "layout_id", word_space_rmse)
) |>
  distinct() |>
  arrange(layout_id)
```

Manual review of these proofs found that all of the layout 3 & 4 options suffer
from some awkward chapter transitions and bad line breaks, and the layout 1
option ends rather awkwardly on a short verso page.

That leaves layout 7!
